title: High-rate USGS well records show coseismic water-level steps above a seismic energy density of about 1e-4 J/m3, but the steps are small (median 1.6 cm) and repeat in the same wells (2008-2025)
abstract: An earlier campaign study found no step excess in daily-mean US well levels after earthquakes; its detection threshold was 0.28 m. We repeated the test with USGS instantaneous (5-60 min) groundwater levels for 666 earthquakes in 2008-2025 (40 large or teleseismic events and 626 regional events). For each well we fitted a trend, tides and a step at the end of the shaking in a 48-h window, scaled the step by fake origins in the same window, and compared the response rate with the same wells in a placebo window 7 days earlier. We removed windows that contain a larger nearby shock. In 225,747 well-windows (5,010 wells, 610 events), the rate of |z| >= 4 steps was equal in earthquake and placebo windows in all six half-decade bins below 1e-4 J/m3 (seismic energy density from the Wang 2007 relation). From 1e-4 J/m3 up, every bin had an excess: 1.97% of 43,368 well-events against 0.81% placebo, growing to 23% against 0% at 0.1 J/m3 or more. The excess occurred only at the wave arrival, not 9-12 h before or after. The median step was 1.6 cm and only 3.6% were 0.28 m or more, which explains the daily-mean null. A well that stepped once stepped again 3.1 times more often than a within-event shuffle predicts (placebo 1.3), and signs repeated in the same well. Rises and falls were equally frequent; static volumetric strain from point moment tensors predicted 73% of signs (95% interval 50-84%) at 1e-9 to 1e-8 strain and 52% at lower strain. The steps are mostly a well-specific dynamic response. Limitations: e is empirical, not measured shaking; 40 of 134 eligible large events were used because of an API rate limit; no barometric correction; the placebo reference and the aftershock rule were added after a first look, and both made the test more conservative.

display.caption: Rate of water-level steps (|z| >= 4) at the seismic-wave arrival against seismic energy density, in earthquake windows (blue) and in placebo windows of the same wells 7 days earlier (orange). Right: excess with 95% event-bootstrap interval. No excess below 1e-4 J/m3; an excess in every half-decade bin above it.
Four example responses (level minus window median). Shaded: masked shaking interval. Ridgecrest 2019, El Mayor-Cucapah 2010, Mineral Virginia 2011, Tehuantepec 2017.

a: sizes of responses at e >= 1e-4 J/m3 (dashed: median 4-sigma detection threshold of this method; orange: median threshold of the daily-mean study). b: agreement of the step sign with the static volumetric strain of a point moment tensor. c: same-well repeat responses relative to a within-event shuffle.
